layers.note: The dominant canopy tree of lowland western Washington; its young trees come up in openings far more than under closed canopy.

moisture.note: Grows from dry to moist ground and dominates well-drained sites; it tolerates saturated or flooded soil poorly, so it drops out on wet ground near water.

heat_load.note: Grows on every aspect and tolerates warm, dry south- and west-facing slopes better than western redcedar or bigleaf maple; only the coolest steep north-east slopes thin it.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in the Olympic Mountains and the west Cascades, where true firs and mountain hemlock take over.

max_slope_deg.note: Roots on steep slopes and rocky ground; thins out on the steepest.

shade_tolerance.note: Intermediate to intolerant of shade near the coast: seedlings need gaps or open ground.
